questions.question: What invariant protects an ML system from silent training-serving mismatch?
options: Training and serving consume data with explicit lineage, time semantics, and reproducible transformations
Every feature is recomputed from scratch for each request
Every event is processed by a streaming engine
Training uses the largest possible historical table
questions.explanation: The invariant makes a feature traceable, reconstructible, and comparable across offline and online consumers. The implementation can still be batch, streaming, or hybrid.

questions.question: Which identity is sufficient to reproduce one daily feature partition?
options: The worker hostname and retry count
The logical interval, input snapshot, transform version, schema version, and parameters
The dashboard timestamp only
The output row count without input identity
questions.explanation: Replay equivalence depends on the logical data and every version that can change its meaning. Attempts and worker hosts are execution details, not the data contract.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the core training-data-management invariant?
options: Every model must use the newest available rows
Every dataset must fit in one storage system
Every model must resolve to an immutable manifest that resolves all training evidence
Every training run must use the same algorithm
questions.explanation: The manifest connects a model to exact sources, transformations, labels, splits, checks, and permissions.

questions.question: A fraud label arrives 30 days after a transaction. Can that label be a feature for the original transaction-time prediction?
options: No, it was unavailable at prediction time and would leak the outcome
Yes, because it is eventually stored
Yes, if the model is tree-based
Only when the label is standardized
questions.explanation: Feature eligibility is defined at prediction time. A later outcome may be the training label, but it cannot be an input to that earlier prediction.

questions.question: A model team changes its tokenizer and re-runs a filter threshold before training. What should be versioned with the resulting dataset manifest?
options: Only the final row count
The source references, transformation code, configuration, and quality report
Only the model checkpoint
The test accuracy from the previous run
questions.explanation: A reproducible dataset release records both its input sources and the transformations that produced the retained examples.

questions.question: Which sequence best protects a held-out evaluation from preprocessing leakage?
options: Fit preprocessing on all rows, split, then train
Split on the deployment boundary, fit preprocessing on training rows, then reuse the frozen state
Tune transformations on test results until the score stabilizes
Create duplicate test rows so every category appears
questions.explanation: The split must happen first. Imputers, scalers, vocabularies, selectors, and other learned transforms fit only on training rows and then transform held-out rows without learning from them.

questions.question: When should data-dependent imputation and scaling statistics be fitted?
options: On the training partition only
On the validation and test partitions together
On every row before the split
Only after production scoring
questions.explanation: Learning transformation state from evaluation rows leaks information into the model-development process.
